1. it will clone the target (public) repo 
2. attempt to copy current sepo (using the latest release version) to the target repo; it will analyze conflicts and then propose a plan to resolve it 
3. then it will submit a pr to the target public repo 

@sepo-agent /answer what's a minimum way for implementing it?

comments.body:
Minimum v1: expose `/install` as a thin alias for the existing `install-agent` skill, not as a new full route engine.

Existing pieces already line up:

- Install docs already define the target behavior: open a PR that copies `.agent/` and `.github/`, merges ignore rules, then runs onboarding/memory/rubrics after merge ([docs](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/docs/deployment/install-existing-repository.md#L5-L47)).
- `.skills/install-agent/SKILL.md` already contains the install workflow, conflict audit, conservative copy rules, validation, and PR body requirements ([skill](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.skills/install-agent/SKILL.md#L1-L157)).
- The router already supports explicit skill execution through `/skill <name>` and runs skills through the shared `skill` job ([router](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/workflows/agent-router.yml#L434-L593)).
- Explicit route parsing is centralized in `triage.ts`, so `/install` can be added in one place as an alias to `{ route: "skill", skill: "install-agent" }` ([parser](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/triage.ts#L107-L136)).
- Source version resolution exists for updates, but it currently filters to non-prerelease stable releases ([resolver](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/scripts/resolve-update-source.sh#L62-L72)). As of today, the only GitHub release I see is `v0.1.0`, marked prerelease, published 2026-05-12, so `/install` should either include prereleases or the current resolver would fall back to `main`.

Proposed minimum implementation:

1. Add `/install` parsing in `extractRequestedRouteDecision()`:
   - Accept `@sepo-agent /install <owner/repo>`.
   - Return `route: "skill"` and `skill: "install-agent"`.
   - Keep `/skill install-agent` working unchanged.

2. Teach `install-agent` to treat workflow-provided context as confirmation:
   - target repo slug from the request text
   - source repo `self-evolving/repo`
   - source ref resolved to latest non-draft release, including prereleases for v0.x while no stable exists
   - branch `agent/install-agent-infra`

3. Add a small source resolver for install:
   - either extend `resolve-update-source.sh` with an `INCLUDE_PRERELEASES=true` mode
   - or create `resolve-install-source.sh` that returns `source_repo`, `source_ref`, `source_sha`, and `release_url`

4. Leave execution on the existing `skill` route:
   - no new workflow needed for the first cut
   - no new `ROUTES` enum entry needed if `/install` maps to `skill`
   - existing access policy applies as `skill`; a later version can add a first-class `install` route if install-specific access policy is needed

5. Add tests:
   - `/install owner/repo` parses to `skill/install-agent`
   - `/skill install-agent` remains unchanged
   - install source resolution selects latest release, including prerelease `v0.1.0`
   - unsupported or malformed target slugs produce a clear answer instead of running

Important v1 limitation: submitting the PR requires auth that can push a branch or fork/open a PR against the target public repo. Minimum safe scope should be: clone any public target, but only open the PR when the resolved Sepo auth token can write to the target or an approved bot/PAT fork path exists. Otherwise, return a clear “install PR cannot be opened until Sepo/App/PAT has target write access” message.

I’d implement this as `/install` → `install-agent` alias first, with release resolution and tests, then consider a dedicated `install` route only if we need separate access policy, metrics, or workflow UI. Please confirm that v1 auth scope is acceptable before coding.

title: Allow a public route `/install` for installing sepo to an existing public repository
